parsedVerdict.reasoning: The infrastructure module has one cohesive concern: adapters connecting the application and domain to outside technology. http.ts is the Express HTTP adapter. createApp delegates every route to the CatalogueService or OrderService passed in through Services. Its order-state checks use the domain's isOrderState and ORDER_STATES, and the shortcut routes (/pay, /pack, /ship, /deliver) call orders.transition instead of re-implementing the transition rules. Domain errors are mapped to HTTP status codes in one place (errorHandler and statusFor). in-memory.ts implements the domain interfaces ProductRepository, OrderRepository, IdGenerator and Clock with no business logic. UuidGenerator and SystemClock don't match the 'in-memory' file name, but they are still infrastructure adapters, so this is a naming issue rather than a split. server.ts is the startup and wiring code: it builds the adapters and services, seeds data through catalogue.addProduct rather than going around the service to the repositories, and starts the server with createApp. The same order-state validation appears twice in http.ts, but both copies read from the single domain source (isOrderState), so it is a small repetition rather than a duplicated invariant.
